extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers and applicants to MRC (UK) funding schemes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for peer reviewers (and applicants) evaluating MRC funding proposals across schemes, using three core criteria (Importance, Scientific Potential, Resources Requested) and a UKRI 1–6 scoring scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance of the research question; Relevance to MRC's strategy; Health/disease/societal impact; Why this research, why now; How the work will fill a critical gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the proposal addresses an important problem, its relevance to MRC strategic priorities, and the potential health, disease or societal impact. Consider whether the case 'why this research, why now' is persuasive and whether the work fills a critical gap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of the research plan; Originality and innovation; Soundness of methodology; Likelihood of achieving stated objectives; Contribution to knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the overall scientific quality: clarity and rigor of the research plan, novelty/innovation, appropriateness and robustness of methods, feasibility of objectives, and expected contribution to knowledge. Look for well‑described methodology and realistic pathways to deliverables and outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources Requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of staffing; Justification for equipment; Realistic budget; Value for money; Adequate time allocation; Suitable institutional environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether requested resources are appropriate and adequately justified (staffing, equipment, time). Determine if the budget is realistic and offers value for money and whether the institutional environment is suitable to deliver the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring System (UKRI 1–6)
rubrics_metrics.description: MRC uses standard UKRI scoring (1 = poor to 6 = exceptional): 6: Exceptional - the application is outstanding; 5: Excellent - very high quality, addresses most criteria to an excellent level; 4: Good - addresses criteria well with some weaknesses; 3: Fair - some merit but significant weaknesses; 2: Weak - flaws that prevent funding; 1: Poor - unsuitable for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the UKRI 1–6 scale to the whole application (across criteria). Use the descriptors to map overall judgement (exceptional through poor) and to communicate the severity/nature of weaknesses or strengths in reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment Process (peer review and panels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are peer reviewed by independent scientific experts from the UK and overseas; detailed information is provided on what reviewers, boards and panels are looking for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are provided by independent experts and considered by MRC boards and panels. Ensure comments align with the core criteria and the expectations communicated to reviewers and panels; be aware that panels/boards interpret reviews in the context of scheme priorities and remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant and Environment Suitability (application guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before applying, applicants should consider each of the specific criteria; whether they fully address each area; whether they, their co-applicants, and their research environment fulfil the required criteria; whether the application meets the strategic priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reviewers and applicants alike: check that the team and research environment have the necessary expertise, track record and infrastructure to deliver the project, that all core criteria are addressed, and that the proposal aligns with MRC strategic priorities.
